title: It Hovers and Hums Like a Hummingbird. It's Not a Bird.
subject: hummingbird hawk-moth

scenes.text: It hovers, it hums, it drinks from flowers mid-air. And it is not a bird.
It's a moth, the hummingbird hawk-moth, and its wings beat around 80 times every second.
That's fast enough that you can actually hear it hum while it hangs in front of a flower.
Its tongue is almost as long as its whole body, and it uncurls it to drink without ever landing.
It works fast too. Up to forty flowers in a single minute, and it flies in bright sunshine, like a bird would.
So that hummingbird in a European garden? Look closer. It has six legs and antennae.

description:
The hummingbird hawk-moth hovers, hums and drinks nectar mid-air, and it is an insect.
Its wings beat around 80 times a second and its tongue is almost as long as its body.
Have you ever mistaken a moth for a bird? Tell us below.
first_comment: Hawk-moths see in full colour and can tell similar flowers apart. Bird or moth: which would you have guessed?
